official.deadline_note: TU Wien publishes no single central scholarship deadline. Each funding route has its own window: Study Grant applications can usually be sent between September and December for the winter semester and between February and May for the summer semester; TU Wien Foundation Grant applications must be sent to stiftungs-stipendium@tuwien.ac.at usually until February; the graduation scholarship for working students is emailed between October and November; the Helmut Veith Stipend invites applications in November; tuition fee waiver applications must be submitted by 31 October for the winter semester and 31 March for the summer semester.
official.application_cycle: Multiple schemes with separate windows; no single central round
official.status_note: TU Wien publishes no single central scholarship round. Its English financial support page lists separate schemes with their own windows, and tuition fee waiver applications run to 31 October for the winter semester and 31 March for the summer semester.
official.tuition_coverage_note: TU Wien does not state that any of its scholarships covers tuition. Instead it publishes a tuition fee waiver mechanism: students can apply for a waiver of the tuition fee for the current semester at the Admission Office, and 'The waiver only includes the tuition fee!'
benefits: Tuition fee waiver: students can apply for a waiver of the tuition fee for the current semester at the Admission Office if there is a valid reason - the waiver only includes the tuition fee, and the ÖH fee must be paid in any case

Merit Scholarship Grants at universities, intended to support students and graduates who have achieved outstanding academic performance in accordance with the study regulations, usually awarded at the end of an academic year
Funding Grants, intended to support scientific or artistic work from students (diploma theses and dissertations)
TU Wien Foundation Grants, awarded to students with social need
Helmut Veith Stipend for female students in the field of computer science who (plan to) pursue one of the Master's programmes in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English
Graduation Scholarship for Working Students, submitable once per academic year for a Bachelor's or Master's study programme
ÖH social funds: social fund, children's fund, housing fund, mediation fund, psychotherapy fund and a fund for students with disabilities
eligibility: Study Grants from the Austrian Study Grant Authority are for students who are Austrian citizens as well as students who fulfil the Austrian citizen status (§ 4 StudFG)
Merit Scholarship Grants are intended for students and graduates who have achieved outstanding academic performance in accordance with the study regulations
TU Wien Foundation Grants are awarded to students with social need

The Helmut Veith Stipend is for female students in the field of computer science who (plan to) pursue one of the Master's programmes in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English and who have (or have the interest to develop) a solid mathematical and technical background in at least one of the areas in which Austrian scientist Helmut Veith worked

Waiver grounds include illness or pregnancy, child care, care of an invalid relative, disability of at least 50%, receipt of a study grant, mobility programmes, stay abroad, reciprocal waiver, and Ukrainian citizenship
requirements: The application for a waiver must be submitted to the Admission Office via Jira until 31 October for the winter semester and 31 March for the summer semester

The required evidence must be submitted as a PDF file in the original or as a notary/court-certified copy; documents not issued in German or English must be translated into German by a court-certified translator and attached
A reason for a waiver that occurred in the past cannot be claimed retrospectively for the current semester
TU Wien Foundation Grant applications must be sent by e-mail to stiftungs-stipendium@tuwien.ac.at, usually until February
The graduation scholarship application must be sent with all required documents by e-mail to abschluss-stipendium@tuwien.ac.at between October and November
documents: For a tuition fee waiver: medical specialist confirmation, birth certificate and confirmation of registration, confirmation of level of care, disability certificate from the Federal Social Office, notification of the study grant authority, or confirmation by the responsible mobility coordinator, depending on the ground claimed
Documents must be PDF files in the original or as notary/court-certified copies
selection_criteria: Merit Scholarship Grants are based on outstanding academic performance in accordance with the study regulations
TU Wien Foundation Grants are based on social need
Tuition fee waivers are granted where a statutory or rectorate-set ground is evidenced within the deadline
coverage: Tuition fee waiver covering the tuition fee only; the ÖH fee must be paid in any case, even if the tuition fee is waived
Tuition fee is €363.36 per semester, or €726.72 per semester for non-EU nationals, plus the ÖH fee including insurance each semester
application_method: Tuition fee waiver: submit the application form to the Admission Office via Jira by 31 October (winter semester) or 31 March (summer semester)
Study Grant: apply through the Austrian Study Grant Authority at stipendium.at, usually September to December for the winter semester and February to May for the summer semester
TU Wien Foundation Grant: email the complete application to stiftungs-stipendium@tuwien.ac.at, usually until February
Graduation scholarship for working students: email the application with all required documents to abschluss-stipendium@tuwien.ac.at between October and November
Helmut Veith Stipend: apply in November via the Helmut Veith Stipend website
Grants for students coming from abroad: search the OeAD GRANTS website at grants.at
official.application_route: Identify the specific scheme you qualify for - the Austrian Study Grant Authority for study grants, the Admission Office via Jira for tuition fee waivers, the dean's offices for merit scholarships and funding grants, or the OeAD grants.at portal for incoming international students - and apply to that body directly.
official.study_mode: Degree programmes at bachelor's, master's and doctoral level; non-degree students pay €363.36 per semester regardless of citizenship
official.citizenship_residency: Study Grants are for Austrian citizens and students who fulfil the Austrian citizen status (§ 4 StudFG). EU, EEA and Swiss citizens, convention refugees, beneficiaries of subsidiary protection and certain third-country nationals with qualifying residence permits are temporarily exempt from tuition fees; citizens of countries listed in Annex 1 of the Decree on Tuition Fee are generally exempt and pay only the ÖH fee. All other non-EU nationals pay €726.72 per semester from the first semester.
official.international_eligibility: Partly. TU Wien itself states 'Grants for Students Coming from Abroad to study at TU Wien can be found on the OeAD's GRANTS website', and degree students from Annex 1 countries and Ukrainian citizens are exempt from tuition fees. However the Austrian Study Grant is limited to Austrian citizens or those fulfilling § 4 StudFG, and non-EU nationals pay tuition from the first semester.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The Helmut Veith Stipend is restricted to female computer science students on an English-taught TU Wien Master's programme in Computer Science; Merit Scholarship Grants and Funding Grants are administered by each dean's office; tuition fee waivers require a specific statutory or rectorate-set ground
official.research_requirement: Funding Grants support scientific or artistic work from students, including diploma theses and dissertations
official.duration: Tuition fee waivers are granted per semester. Study Grant support is per semester, with successful academic performance of at least 14 semester hours per week (SWS) or 30 ECTS credits required to be proven after two semesters.
official.description: TU Wien publishes an overview of existing financial support rather than a single scholarship: Study Grants from the Austrian Study Grant Authority, Merit Scholarship Grants and Funding Grants administered by the dean's offices, TU Wien Foundation Grants for students with social need, the Helmut Veith Stipend for female computer science master's students, graduation scholarships, and ÖH social funds.
official.program_type: Portfolio of grants, scholarships and tuition fee waivers - no single central scholarship

individual Merit Scholarship Grant and Funding Grant amounts and deadlines, which are published by the dean's offices and on the German-only Admissions Office site
any English language requirement for these funding routes

applicant_utility.summary: There is no single TU Wien scholarship to apply for, so the real task is working out which of the several published routes you actually qualify for - and they have completely different windows, from November for the Helmut Veith Stipend to 31 October and 31 March for tuition fee waivers. If you are a non-EU national the headline cost is the €726.72 per semester tuition fee plus the ÖH fee, so the tuition fee waiver, not a scholarship, is usually the mechanism that matters most. The Austrian Study Grant is effectively closed to you unless you hold Austrian citizenship or fulfil § 4 StudFG, so incoming international students should look at the OeAD grants.at portal instead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Female computer science master's students on the English-taught programme, students with documented social need, and non-EU students with a specific statutory ground for a tuition fee waiver.
application_readiness_checklist: Work out your tuition fee status first - €363.36 or €726.72 per semester plus the ÖH fee depending on nationality and residence title
Check whether your country appears in Annex 1 of the Decree on Tuition Fee, which makes you generally exempt and liable only for the ÖH fee

If you are claiming a tuition fee waiver, apply via the Admission Office Jira portal before 31 October (winter) or 31 March (summer) - the reason must be evidenced in the current semester and cannot be claimed retrospectively
If you are an incoming international student, search grants.at rather than expecting a TU Wien scholarship
If you are a female CS master's student, prepare your Helmut Veith Stipend application for the November window
common_rejection_risks: Missing the waiver deadline because the reason arose in an earlier semester and cannot be claimed retrospectively
Assuming the tuition fee waiver also removes the ÖH fee, which must be paid in any case
Submitting documents that are not PDFs in the original or notary/court-certified copies, or German translations that are not court-certified
Applying for the Austrian Study Grant as a non-Austrian citizen who does not fulfil § 4 StudFG
Expecting a Merit Scholarship Grant amount or deadline from the central page when these are set by each dean's office
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: For non-EU nationals, €726.72 per semester tuition plus the ÖH fee including insurance; plus Vienna living costs, which none of the published TU Wien routes cover.
document_audit: Waiver evidence must be a PDF, original or notary/court-certified, with court-certified German translations for documents not in German or English
A disability of at least 50% requires a disability certificate from the Federal Social Office
Receipt of a study grant in the previous or current semester is itself a waiver ground, proven by notification from the study grant authority
Students with Ukrainian citizenship have tuition fees waived automatically with no separate application required
alerts: Students employed by TU Wien in the past semester for at least 90 days at 20 hours or more per week, and doctoral students employed at 20 hours or more per week, usually have waivers entered automatically
Students with an Austrian residence title 'Aufenthaltsbewilligung Studierender' are exempt from waivers on the grounds of illness, pregnancy, child care and care of an invalid relative
Reimbursement of tuition fees runs to the following 28/29 February for the winter semester and 30 September for the summer semester
Students who spend at least one semester as a student representative can have tuition waived for up to four semesters depending on the position held
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Choose the specific scheme, then apply to the responsible body - Austrian Study Grant Authority for study grants, the Admission Office via Jira for waivers, the relevant dean's office for merit and funding grants, or OeAD grants.at for incoming international students.

official.deadline_note: The Spring Semester scholarship application period for newly admitted students begins on 1 October and the application deadline is 30 November at 13:00 CET. The Fall Semester application period begins 1 March and closes 31 May at 13:00 CET. The Austrian Federal Ministry merit award separately closes 4 December 2026 at 1 p.m. CET.

applicant_utility.summary: Admission comes first - you cannot apply for this scholarship until you have been admitted to a full degree program, and the application form itself has to be requested from the Admissions Office rather than downloaded. The financial need component is not a formality: you must produce official translated evidence of net earnings in euros, and bank statements are explicitly refused, so plan how you will document household income. Aim at the Distinction level by pairing a 3.5+ GPA with C1 English, because that is what separates a 12,000 euro award from 4,000.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Newly admitted bachelor's or master's students with a 3.0+ GPA, C1 or B2 English, a genuine documented financial need, and the ability to write a 1,000-1,200 word essay in English.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure admission to a full bachelor's or master's degree program - certificate and English preparation programs are not eligible
Email admissions@webster.ac.au to request the online scholarship application form once the period has opened
Gather official net earnings documentation with certified English translations and convert all amounts to euros, noting the rate used
Write the 1,000 to 1,200 word English essay on one of the two published topics before starting the form
Confirm your GPA on the American 4.0 scale and your CEFR English level so you know which award level you are targeting
common_rejection_risks: Applying before admission is confirmed, since the acceptance letter is a required upload
Submitting bank account statements as financial evidence, which are not accepted
Submitting financial documents in a language other than English without an official translation, or with amounts not converted to euros
An essay outside the 1,000 to 1,200 word range
Letting the GPA fall below 3.0 in any semester, which ends renewal
Applying while enrolled in a certificate or English preparation program
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: All Vienna living costs, accommodation, insurance and travel, plus the balance of tuition above the partial scholarship - Webster Vienna states plainly that the remaining tuition fee must be paid by the recipient.
document_audit: The financial motivation letter must cover your financial background, how the scholarship would help and why you deserve it - a generic statement will not carry the financial need test
Official financial documents must be officially translated into English if not already in English, with all amounts in euros and the conversion rate indicated
For self-employed applicants, submit the company information and an official letter stating net earnings in euros instead of salary slips
The Fall 2026 application period for the Webster Vienna Training Scholarship is closed, so that route is not currently available to enrolled students
alerts: Deadlines are at 13:00 CET, not midnight - 30 November for the Spring round and 31 May for the Fall round
Renewal requires 24 US credits or 48 ECTS per year for undergraduate and 12 US credits or 30 ECTS per year for graduate, plus a 3.0 GPA each semester

US citizens can additionally complete FAFSA with the Webster University code 002521 by 1 March for maximum consideration, but Federal Financial Aid cannot award 100% of demonstrated need and is not disbursed until studies begin
The Austrian Federal Ministry merit award of 1,000 to 1,500 euros closes 4 December 2026 at 1 p.m. CET and requires a 3.3 GPA plus credit thresholds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Be admitted to a full degree program, request the online form from the Admissions Office, complete it with all documents uploaded, and await the level decision before your first semester.
